questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to discover a culture and academic difference then my own.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I was very difficult. I felt like I didn't get any information from the university about anything. They only send some flyers out by email that was outdated.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As mention, it was acutely quite bad. They gave us half an hour where we could ask questions, but it was only academic questions. they didn't do introduction week to meet other people. they didn't really prepare us before academically either, as we found out that there were some classes we weren't allowed to take. In general, it was really difficult to get any information, so as eramus student you really tried to get any information from everyone, but the hardest part was that you didn't know any other Erasmus student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: As a dane it was easy, because there is a lot of Danes renting out to Danes. But I know that it was difficult for many others.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Be in good time when applying for housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They gave us a lot of different papers that you had to fill out. and they only wanted by hand which is weird as a dane, when you coming from a very digitalized university. Additionally, it was very difficult for me to convince them to take English classes, even though I speak better English then French. But if you persistent, you will eventually get you will. Also, the information on the classes online are outdated, and the course description is not something they use a lot, but just write to the professors and ask for it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I had mostly problems with my own university, because they were 6 weeks for them respond, and the host institution had not there classes ready before the semester actually started. This meant that I almost gave up on my eramus exchange in the beginning, because I couldn't get my Erasmus "scholarship". 
ULB has two weeks were you can try classes, before you can even sign up for them. This does not work with the Erasmus application and the deadlines at all.
When I finally got the classes at ULB that I wanted (after a lot of convincing of me wanting English speaking classes), I had to wait 6 weeks for Copenhagen University to respond. Here I had a deadline at ULB at 2 weeks, and also had a eramus deadline. This lead into that I blinded had to trust that Copenhagen would approve, and I didn't have a Learning Agreement in the begning. This stressed me out so much!

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I wouldn't say that they help. it was more me trying to convince them that I was qualified enough to have masterclasses, even though I'm a bachelor student. It took a lot of convincing, but they eventually agreed because I was a third year bachelor student, and I spoke good English.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I eventually got all the classes that I need for getting a Learning Agreement. It wasn't all the classes I wanted - especially because it would make so much more sense that only had masterclasses, but they wouldn't let me at political science. I do know, however, that the law faculty allowed bachelor student to only taking law classes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can only English classes, you just have to persistent. Write to your own university first, and make a plan A; B; C; D; etc. Because you really have to fight for it. But I would say that ULB is trying to be helpful as possible.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would say that classes wasn't were I was challenged. Only the French class.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think, because im a third year bachelor student from Copenhagen - most of the bachelor classes had elements that I had have before. It was mostly challenging to understand how I was supposed to study for the exam, because ULB mostly have Multiple choice exam. My most challenging Classe was a law class, because I don't study law.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It depends on the teacher. Most classes was only lectures that looks like Copenhagens. One teacher made us make presentations the whole semester. And we weren't allowed to take any seminars.

One of my teacher taught both in Introduction to EU politics and Decision making in the EU. One is bachelor class, and one is master class. However, it was the same syllabus and classes.

questions.answer: a lot of sport was available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't take any, because I was too afraid with the French.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I visited a lot of other cities nearby, and I would recommend that. Bruxelles is more a food kind of city - so they have good food, and few sighting seeing. they do, however, have tons of museums!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think that was okay, I would say. Kind of what you could expect. Bruxelles is also a city full of other countries cultures, so its pretty easy to adapt to whatever you like.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go the ESN events, and follow them on instagram, and really try to just go up to people and ask if they are Erasmus student, and ask if they know anything. You really have to fight to get to know anyone.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don't think I found any cultural difference difficult. to me it was nice to se how Belgians do it. It is very French in Bruxelles to be honest.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That were so many different cultures in one city, and you could get anything from all over the world in just one city.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
be persistent. 
discover other cities.
And ask ULB whenever you have a problem with deadlines, they are more flexible. 
And you can find classes in English and get them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The exam is by hand and with a ball pen "kuglepen" which nobody had told before it sat at the exam.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The experience of seeing how a university (French speaking) in Belgium teach and learn.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The whole learning agreement procedure, and finding Erasmus students.

Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
